paragraphs.text: Shipment MZN-10-07 occurred at Manzanillo on 2010-06-05. A taxi operator who works the Manzanillo waterfront reported moving a group of men between the container terminal and a hotel on the harbor road over several evenings in early June. The operator believed the men were arranging a shipment because they discussed container numbers and truck schedules in the cab, but could not identify them and did not hear the name of any organization. The reporting office has no basis to link the activity to a known network.

The operator described the men as well dressed and as paying in cash with large bills. On one trip they were joined by a woman who was introduced as an accountant. The operator stated that the hotel in question is used by legitimate shipping agents and by crews waiting for berths, and that the presence of such a group there is not unusual. The operator has reported on waterfront movements before and has been accurate on times and places but has never been able to identify individuals. The operator added that the group tipped generously and asked to be dropped at a side entrance rather than the lobby, which the operator found unusual for shipping agents but not for crews avoiding a hotel manager who knows them.

The reporting office assesses this as low-value background on the harbor district rather than as information on a specific load. The source has no known motive to fabricate the details reported here. The reporting office cannot exclude that the group was engaged in legitimate shipping business. The account is retained because the hotel in question appears in other reporting on the port and a pattern may emerge over time.
